title.narrative: Sustainable charcoal production and cooking stoves in central Liberia

description.narrative: In Liberia, approximately 70 per cent of households do not have access to electricity and rely on fuelwood and charcoal for cooking. Particularly in rural areas, the widespread cooking practice with solid fuels causes severe implications for human health, forest degradation, and climate change. This project improved rural households' access to energy-efficient cookstoves and improved charcoal production technology to mitigate Green House Gas (GHG) emissions, reduce deforestation, and improve health and rural livelihoods in Bong County, Central Liberia. The project directly benefitted 1,000 rural households and two charcoal associations. The targeted households were in three townships. Especially low-income households that were either headed by women or children have benefitted from the project.
